flags: minor: difference-quotient form f(x+h)-f(x) is more precalculus-flavored than typical SAT, though still within nonlinear functions/equivalent expressions
Q089-01.notes: 3(x+h)^2-2-(3x^2-2)=6xh+3h^2. A drops cross term, C/D mishandle constants.

flags: minor: classic contest pairing trick (x(x+4))((x+1)(x+3)); calculator users can solve x=-2±sqrt(10) and substitute, which lowers difficulty somewhat
Q089-03.notes: x(x+4)=6, (x+1)(x+3)=x^2+4x+3=9; product 54. Verified both roots give 54.

Q089-04.notes: Expression = x+k for x≠k; 4+k=10, k=6; x=4≠k so defined.

Q089-05.notes: Below axis on (1,5); decreasing for x<3 (vertex at 3). Intersection 1<x<3. Graphing makes it quick.

flags: minor: 8-15-17 triple plus well-known median-to-hypotenuse fact; 120/17 (altitude) is a good distractor
Q089-07.notes: AB=17; midpoint of hypotenuse is circumcenter so CM=17/2=8.5.

Q089-08.notes: Center (4,4), half-diagonal (3,2); rotate 90°: (−2,3) -> vertices (2,7) and (6,1). C (1,6) is the axis-aligned rectangle trap. Checked others not equidistant/perpendicular.

Q089-10.notes: Half lateral 30π + two half-discs 9π + rectangular cut face 6×10=60 -> 39π+60. B omits ends, D uses full discs, A uses 3×10 for cut face.

Q089-11.notes: A(0,0),B(8,0),C(8,8),D(0,8),E(8,6). AE=10; angle DAE complements angle BAE; sin(DAE)=cos(BAE)=8/10=0.8. 0.6 trap is sin(BAE), 0.75 is tan.
